angle: Michael Corleone's descent from decorated war hero to ruthless crime boss.
hook: Michael Corleone was a decorated Marine hero before becoming a Mafia don.
points: In The Godfather, Michael initially enrolls in Dartmouth to escape his family's criminal enterprise.
He enters the Mafia world only after a drug kingpin attempts to assassinate his father.
Michael kills a police captain to protect his father, breaking a long-standing Mafia rule.
His ruthless rise to power ultimately destroys his own family, leading to his wife leaving him.
The lesson: Pursuing power at the cost of your integrity leaves you isolated and spiritually bankrupt.
closer: What is the true cost of the empire you are building?

evidence.hook: For his bravery in battle, Michael is awarded the Navy Cross and featured in Life magazine in 1944.
points: Michael initially wants nothing to do with the Corleone "family business", and enrolls at Dartmouth College in order to escape any potential involvement in crime.
Just before Christmas 1945, Vito is critically wounded in an assassination attempt by drug kingpin Virgil Sollozzo (Al Lettieri), pushing Michael into the Mafia world he has avoided for so long.
Hagen warns that killing McCluskey would violate a long-standing Mafia rule not to kill police officers, and says it would incite deadly backlash from rival Mafia families
Kay decides to leave Michael and take their children with her, believing Michael will always live in a world of crime and violence.
Weary of the bloody, lonely life of a Don, Michael retires, making Vincent his successor

caption: Michael Corleone began as a man who wanted to escape his father's shadow, only to become the very thing he despised. He gained the world but lost his soul and his family in the process. Is your ambition serving your purpose or destroying your peace?
